headline: Gang threatens embassies in Dhaka to extort money
summary: The Detective Branch of the DMP has revealed that a criminal gang is targeting foreign missions, including those of China, Pakistan, and Turkey, to create panic and extort money.
details: A criminal gang has been sending threat emails to various embassies in Dhaka's diplomatic zone, according to DMP Additional Commissioner (Detective Branch) Shafiqul Islam.
The gang used bKash numbers of ordinary people in the emails to attempt extortion, effectively masking their identities.
Police have questioned three to four individuals whose numbers were used, but these people claimed they had no knowledge of the the threats.
The threat emails were sent to four foreign embassies, including those of China, Pakistan, and Turkey, as well as several government offices.
DB chief Shafiqul Islam stated that the preliminary assessment suggests the gang's goals may extend beyond money.
Authorities believe the gang may be attempting to create panic among foreign ambassadors and diplomatic missions to tarnish the country's image.
caption:
Foreign embassies in Dhaka, including China, Pakistan, and Turkey, have been targeted by threat emails from a criminal gang.

A criminal gang has been sending threat emails to various embassies in Dhaka's diplomatic zone, according to DMP Additional Commissioner (Detective Branch) Shafiqul Islam.

The gang used bKash numbers of ordinary people in the emails to attempt extortion, effectively masking their identities.

Police have questioned three to four individuals whose numbers were used, but these people claimed they had no knowledge of the the threats.

The threat emails were sent to four foreign embassies, including those of China, Pakistan, and Turkey, as well as several government offices.

DB chief Shafiqul Islam stated that the preliminary assessment suggests the gang's goals may extend beyond money.

Authorities believe the gang may be attempting to create panic among foreign ambassadors and diplomatic missions to tarnish the country's image.

headline_marked: Air Force officer [[sent to jail by ICT]] over Ilias Ali disappearance
headline: Air Force officer sent to jail by ICT over Ilias Ali disappearance
summary: Wing Commander Saifur Rahman Saif is detained in a crimes against humanity case involving the 2012 enforced disappearance of BNP leader M Ilias Ali.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-1 has sent Wing Commander Saifur Rahman Saif of the Bangladesh Air Force to jail.
The order was passed in open court after Saifur was shown arrested in a connection to the crimes against humanity case regarding the enforced disappearance of BNP leader M Ilias Ali.
The tribunal had previously issued an arrest warrant against the officer, and authorities were ordered to produce him before the court.
According to the prosecution, the case is currently in the investigation stage.
M Ilias Ali, then organising secretary of BNP's Sylhet division, and his driver, Ansar, went missing on the night of April 17, 2012.
Ilias Ali was a former general secretary of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal and a two-time Member of Parliament from the Sylhet-2 constituency.
caption:
An Air Force officer has been sent to jail by the International Crimes Tribunal for his alleged role in the disappearance of a BNP leader.

The International Crimes Tribunal-1 has sent Wing Commander Saifur Rahman Saif of the Bangladesh Air Force to jail.

The order was passed in open court after Saifur was shown arrested in a connection to the crimes against humanity case regarding the enforced disappearance of BNP leader M Ilias Ali.

The tribunal had previously issued an arrest warrant against the officer, and authorities were ordered to produce him before the court.

According to the prosecution, the case is currently in the investigation stage.

M Ilias Ali, then organising secretary of BNP's Sylhet division, and his driver, Ansar, went missing on the night of April 17, 2012.

Ilias Ali was a former general secretary of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal and a two-time Member of Parliament from the Sylhet-2 constituency.

Source: Somoy News, The Daily Star
